items.title: From drought to deluge: ‘Super’ El Niño’s expanding reach
items.summary: Across Papua New Guinea, water sources are drying up, crops are failing and food prices are rising months before the worst agricultural impacts are expected. Behind those warning signs is an El Niño whose Pacific Ocean temperatures have already surpassed the equivalent measurements during the historic 1997 and 2015 events – part of an unfolding climate pattern being dubbed a “Super El Niño” by some climate watchers.

items.title: Five Energy Market Factors That Could Tip the Scales in the Middle East War
items.summary: Oil, gas and fuel prices are central to the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran, with Washington striving to lower them and Tehran to keep them high. With both sides determined to prevail, five market-shaping developments in particular could affect whether fighting ramps up or de-escalates.

items.summary: Intense fighting in Yemen has forced more than 184,000 people from their homes since the start of August, most of them since early September, the UN migration agency (IOM) said on Monday.

items.title: Israeli demolition in East Jerusalem displaces 69 Palestinians
items.summary: Sixty-nine Palestinians – more than half of them children – were displaced on Tuesday after Israeli authorities green lit the demolition of their residential building in the At Tur area of East Jerusalem, the UN aid coordination office (OCHA) has reported.

items.title: ‘The clock on AI regulation is ticking’, warns UN rights chief
items.summary: The world is running out of time to put guardrails on artificial intelligence, UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk warned Monday, as a “ruthless race” between companies and countries raises concerns about human safety and even humanity’s survival.

items.title: Extreme heat making pregnancy a ‘new fault line’ in climate crisis
items.summary: Pregnancy and childbirth have become a “new fault line in the global climate crisis” as extreme heat worsens, the head of the UN climate action body (UNFCCC) warned on Monday, calling for maternal and newborn health to be built into countries’ climate plans.

items.title: ICC unseals four arrest warrants over Taliban persecution of women and girls
items.summary: The International Criminal Court (ICC) has made public four arrest warrants against senior Taliban figures, accusing them of persecuting women and girls in Afghanistan, which amounts to a crime against humanity.

items.summary: The Department of Veterans Affairs and War Department have jointly released a clinical practice guideline to help clinicians provide improved care for women experiencing perimenopause and menopause.

items.title: Lack of Access to Financing Impedes, Reverses Development, Climate Action, Delegates Warn as Second Committee Continues Its General Debate

items.title: Oversight Bodies Critical to Making UN More Agile, Coherent, Cost-Effective, Speakers Tell Fifth Committee
items.summary: As the United Nations undergoes a profound reform meant to increase its agility while spending less, the role of its oversight bodies is critical to assess the accompanying risks, delegates in the Fifth Committee (Administrative and Budgetary) warned today.

items.title: The U.S.-led Anti-ISIS Coalition is Leaving Iraq: What Happens Next?
items.summary: The coming withdrawal of U.S.-led coalition forces marks a significant moment in Iraq’s tumultuous recent history. Yet with the Middle East war bringing conflict to the country and questions surrounding the state’s capacity to assert its authority, the significance is mainly symbolic.
